# **Poster Requirements**

**Links:** [Home](https://github.com/txt/se26f/blob/main/README.md) · [Project 1a](https://github.com/txt/se26f/blob/main/docs/submit/1/proj1a.md) · [Project 1b](https://github.com/txt/se26f/blob/main/docs/submit/1/proj1b.md) · [Use case format](https://github.com/txt/se26f/blob/main/docs/submit/1/usecases0.md) · [Prior projects](https://drive.google.com/drive/u/2/folders/1dGGQNCWC3BakD-nUZn5vPecPdm0KAhXA)

Only [Project 1b](https://github.com/txt/se26f/blob/main/docs/submit/1/proj1b.md) hands in a poster (as a PDF, to Moodle). [Project 1a](https://github.com/txt/se26f/blob/main/docs/submit/1/proj1a.md) has no poster. The poster sells the **better product** you propose — with the [Project 1a](https://github.com/txt/se26f/blob/main/docs/submit/1/proj1a.md) findings (use cases, tests) as its "before" evidence.

## **Format**

* Use one standard page (letter or A4).  
* You can use small fonts (4 to 6 points).  
* Submit one PDF file to Moodle.  
* Do not leave large empty areas.  
* Make it exciting. Keep it professional.

## **Content**

The poster must show:

* Your group number.  
* The names of all group members.  
* A mission statement paragraph. Give the **why** (the challenge you answer), the **what** (the thing you will build), and the **so what** (the benefits). Example: "Online content can be emotionally overwhelming. Our app helps make sense of it. Sentiment Analyzer Pro lets users analyze the emotional tone of text, images, news, speech, and YouTube comments. Whether you track brand sentiment, filter negativity, or just stay informed, the app makes emotional insight fast and accessible. With a Chrome extension and improved UI, it is now easier than ever to understand how content feels, not just what it says."  
* The stakeholders (for example: admin, staff, customer — who else?). These can be part of the mission statement.  
* QR codes, each with its URL printed underneath (so we can work from the QR code or from the URL), for:  
  * Your repository.  
  * Your discussion forum. The forum can be private, but CSC 510 tutors and lecturers must have access.  
  * The feature walk-through video (2 to 5 minutes). How you host the video is your choice.  
* Icons that show your proposed tech stack.  
* Small screen snaps of the system. If your system is a CLI tool, show one call to the tool and its printed output.

## **The demo**

Projects 2 and 3 each include one live demo, worth 5 of that project's marks. (Project 1a needs a demo video only; Project 1b has no demo — its product is not built yet.) Be prepared to demo the running system when asked. For that demo:

* Show up with the software already installed and running (on your laptop, or on the cloud). The demo must start straight away. No setup time.  
* Provide one operator for the demo. The tutor watches the operator run the code.  
* Demo scheduling rules (working hours, and optional after-hours slots): see the [policies](https://github.com/txt/se26f/blob/main/docs/submit/lect/policies.md).

## **Sample posters**

Samples from past years are here: [https://drive.google.com/drive/u/2/folders/1dGGQNCWC3BakD-nUZn5vPecPdm0KAhXA](https://drive.google.com/drive/u/2/folders/1dGGQNCWC3BakD-nUZn5vPecPdm0KAhXA)

**Warning:** our standard for posters has changed for 2026\. Use the samples for inspiration only. Do not follow them verbatim. This page is the standard. In particular, these older posters may lack: URLs printed under every QR code; milestones grouped Before / Now / Future; and (for Project 1b) selling the PROPOSED product — the samples below sell finished work, your 1b poster sells a plan.

Three strong ones from Fall '25, and what to copy from each:

![Epicourier poster: mission, nutrient command center, gamified wellness, 1130+ tests][image1]

**Epicourier** — copy: the mission statement (why/what/so-what in one paragraph), stakeholder list with a reason each cares, and a test count stated plainly (1,130+ automated tests, CI/CD).

![Wolfbite WIC scanner poster: clear tagline, test screenshot, three QR codes][image2]

**Wolfbite** — copy: the 15-second sell ("Scan smarter. Shop faster. Stress less." — you know the product before reading a paragraph), the visible test run (57/57 passing, screenshot not claim), and three labeled QR codes.

![Howl2Go poster: stakeholders, existing versus new features, future improvements, 300+ tests][image3]

**Howl2Go** — copy: the past / present / future structure (existing features → implementation updates → future improvements — closest of the three to our Before/Now/Future rule), and concrete feature lines ("7 micronutrients across 1,150+ items", not "improved nutrition").

## **Milestones**

Show three groups of milestones. Each group has 3 to 5 milestones. Each milestone must have a clear goal and a possible implementation plan.

* **Before:** the work that was done before (Project 1a).  
* **Now:** the work you plan for this month (Project 2).  
* **Future:** the work that is possible in the next month (Project 3).

Be ambitious. Dull milestones lose marks. But do not be too ambitious — you must code this.

## **Sell the software**

* Show what is better now, because this code was written.  
* Propose the better version (version i+1).  
* Boast your test cases from Project 1a.

## **Ways to lose points**

* The poster or the demo does not have the features above.  
* The poster does not sell the project:  
  * After 15 seconds, a reader still does not know what the project is about.  
  * The poster gives no good reason to care about the tech stack (for example: "Select this project to learn Kubernetes").  
* You have too few test cases.
